research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
methodological_questions: Is a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across split halves or across seasons?
How many team-seasons or games are needed to detect a reliable defensive trait given half-level noise?
Does regression to the mean or selection of extreme team-seasons inflate apparent reliability?
How can defensive effects be separated from opponent quality, pace, and game-state (halftime margin) confounders in H2-H1 change?

historical_evidence.finding: Crunch-time PPP-delta identity stability year over year: YoY r = -0.023 on 62 pairs; per-team-season crunch samples of about 100+ possessions mean deltas of ±0.05 PPP fall within sampling noise. Recorded verdict: null, failure type A_unanswerable.

Structural concentration vs defensive vulnerability: C1a rho=+0.079, p=0.0882, CI[-0.114,+0.234]; C1b rho=+0.095, p=0.0738; robust 0.2/0.3 variants also fail. n=117 across 30 franchises. Recorded as B_powered_null, with the CI spanning zero.

Opponent-relative leverage sweep over 870 ordered team pairs: exploit available 33.3%, trap 23.3%, neither 50.0%, median best edge 3.79%. The record notes that edges depend only on the defense (for example DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they are not matchup-specific. This is descriptive and concerns play-type points per possession, not H2-H1 change.

Coverage feasibility gate on 90 team-seasons with ≥200 possessions in both halves of the comparison: |rho(COVERED,TALENT)|=0.042, aux R2=0.203, rho(TALENT,PPP)=+0.027. This is a feasibility gate on talent control, not a test of H2-H1 reliability.

Within-game adaptation by halftime margin, crunch time, and post-run: OTHER +2.26 to +2.48pp in H2 in every bucket. The record states the OTHER label is known to be noisy (PT audit). No inferential tests were run.

Defensive scheme change inferred from labels: within-game change 319/523 (61.0%), cross-game change 298/440 (67.7%), transition matrices near-uniform. The record's caveat is that inferred labels cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently. Recorded failure LABEL_ERROR.
On-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH): confident label rates 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60); switches_on not populated. Verdict: failed_gate.

No systematic pivots when a better same-game option exists: 1,466/1,539 (95.3%) had a better option; zero significant pivots in the paper analysis. Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Relevant to game-state dynamics, not to defense.
Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games: team AVOID% ranges 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC); BEST% 0.0%-15.8%; player samples 10-178 possessions. Descriptive only.
Player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 PPP gaps across 78 players with ≥5 rows per tier: large gaps appear for some players with small n, and some reverse. The record notes no multiplicity or clustered test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a team-level trait for stability year over year using a sub-game split of team-season performance (crunch-time PPP delta).
failed_approaches.why: YoY r = -0.023 on 62 pairs; per-team-season samples of about 100+ possessions were too noisy, so ±0.05 PPP deltas sat within sampling noise (recorded as A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive schemes (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields to create a defensive-trait variable.
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates were 14.9% and 3.3%, switches_on was unpopulated, and the gate failed. The record cites label error and small samples.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring defensive adjustment through inferred scheme-change labels.
failed_approaches.why: The label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution, and near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise (recorded as untestable, LABEL_ERROR).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 PPP gap as evidence of counter effectiveness.
failed_approaches.why: Samples per player were small (single-game playsheets), with no multiplicity or clustered test. The record flags placebo dependence, and some gaps reverse.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Team-level structural measure as a predictor of defensive vulnerability across 30 franchises.
failed_approaches.why: Null with a CI spanning zero (n=117, 30 franchises), recorded as B_powered_null with low power and a large minimum detectable effect.

evidence_establishes: Within this project's records, every team-level defensive or trait-stability test that was run on a sub-game or inferred measure was null, untestable, or failed a gate. None of the records supports a reliable team defensive trait.
Sub-game team-season samples of around 100 possessions (FAM:SF-APPA-029) produce deltas within sampling noise, which is a direct warning for the noise level of a half-level H2-H1 measure.

Team-level structural and defensive measures across roughly 30 franchises gave null results with wide confidence intervals (FAM:SF-PAP-024), so the design needs a much larger effective sample or a far less noisy outcome to detect modest effects.

Defensive play-type edges in FAM:SF-APPA-034 are defense-specific rather than matchup-specific. This suggests some defense-level structure exists, but it was measured on points per possession by play type, not on H2-H1 change.
A talent-control gate (FAM:SF-PAP-009) passed with 90 team-seasons, so talent confounding can be partly addressed in this data.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests the defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change, or the year-over-year or split-half reliability of that effect.
No record gives the variance decomposition needed to estimate the reliability of a team's H2-H1 defensive effect.
No record shows whether halftime-margin or garbage-time game-state effects can be separated from a defensive effect in H2-H1 differences.
The retrieved records do not show that the 120 team-seasons in the stated data are sufficient for a reliability estimate of this outcome.
No record establishes whether the best/avoid counter framing applies to the H2-H1 outcome.
own_inferences: Half-level opponent point differentials are noisy. My rough estimate is that a team's H2-H1 defensive effect over one season has a sampling SE on the order of 1 point per game, which is likely large relative to plausible true between-team differences. This is an inference, not a recorded result.
The 120 team-seasons are unlikely to reach useful power for reliability unless the outcome is aggregated across many games per team-season and the between-team variance is actually substantial.
Game-state (halftime margin, garbage time, pace) is probably the dominant confounder of H2-H1 change, so any defensive effect must be estimated after conditioning on halftime margin.
Prior team-level null results in this project suggest the trait-reliability hypothesis is more likely to fail than to be supported, unless the between-team variance is large.
uncertainties: The true between-team variance of the H2-H1 defensive effect is unknown; the reliability could be near zero.
The exact number of games per team-season in the stated data and any missing playoff games are not stated, so the effective sample is unknown.
Whether the stated data fields (play-by-play, substitution intervals, matchup minutes) support a clean halftime-margin and garbage-time control is not established by any retrieved record.

The retrieved records do not show which team-seasons are complete. The 2025-26 regular season is only complete from 2026-04-13 and the 2025-26 playoffs from 2026-06-21, which bears on whether those seasons can be used.
The search returned only 10 records, none on H2-H1 reliability directly; further search for direct records was not run.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that team-level sub-game trait tests in this project have repeatedly failed or returned null (SF-APPA-029, SF-PAP-024, SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-005). That lowered my prior that a 120-team-season H2-H1 defensive trait is measurable with useful power and led me to make the decision conditional on a feasibility gate. Without this evidence I would have proposed the full reliability study. The defense-specific structure in SF-APPA-034 keeps the question open rather than closing it.

how many team-seasons are needed to detect a reliable defensive trait given noise in half-level differences

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
